audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 4 draft aligned to Ebenezer battle, ark capture, deaths of Hophni and Phinehas, Eli's death, and Ichabod naming; later source/witness audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: Word of Samuel came to all Israel. Israel went out to meet Philistines for battle and camped beside Ebenezer, while Philistines camped at Aphek.

familiar.text: And the word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and pitched beside Ebenezer: and the Philistines pitched in Aphek.

verses.restored: Philistines arranged themselves to meet Israel. Battle spread, and Israel was struck before Philistines; they struck down in battle line in field about four thousand men.

familiar.text: And the Philistines put themselves in array against Israel: and when they joined battle, Israel was smitten before the Philistines: and they slew of the army in the field about four thousand men.

verses.restored: The people came to camp, and elders of Israel said, Why has YHWH struck us today before Philistines? Let us take to ourselves from Shiloh ark of covenant of YHWH, so it may come among us and deliver us from palm of our enemies.

familiar.text: And when the people were come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, Wherefore hath the LORD smitten us to day before the Philistines? Let us fetch the ark of the covenant of the LORD out of Shiloh unto us, that, when it cometh among us, it may save us out of the hand of our enemies.

verses.restored: The people sent to Shiloh and carried from there ark of covenant of YHWH of armies, one sitting above cherubim. The two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with ark of covenant of God.

familiar.text: So the people sent to Shiloh, that they might bring from thence the ark of the covenant of the LORD of hosts, which dwelleth between the cherubims: and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God.

verses.restored: When ark of covenant of YHWH came to camp, all Israel shouted a great shout, and earth resounded.

familiar.text: And when the ark of the covenant of the LORD came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth rang again.

verses.restored: Philistines heard sound of shout and said, What is sound of this great shout in camp of Hebrews? They learned that ark of YHWH had come to camp.

familiar.text: And when the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, What meaneth the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews? And they understood that the ark of the LORD was come into the camp.

verses.restored: Philistines were afraid, for they said, A god has come to camp. They said, Woe to us, for there has not been such as this before.

familiar.text: And the Philistines were afraid, for they said, God is come into the camp. And they said, Woe unto us! for there hath not been such a thing heretofore.

verses.restored: Woe to us! Who will rescue us from hand of these mighty gods? These are gods who struck Egyptians with every blow in wilderness.

familiar.text: Woe unto us! who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty Gods? these are the Gods that smote the Egyptians with all the plagues in the wilderness.

verses.restored: Strengthen yourselves and become men, Philistines, lest you serve Hebrews as they served you. Become men and fight.

familiar.text: Be strong, and quit yourselves like men, O ye Philistines, that ye be not servants unto the Hebrews, as they have been to you: quit yourselves like men, and fight.

verses.restored: Philistines fought. Israel was struck, and each fled to his tents. The striking was very great; from Israel thirty thousand foot soldiers fell.

familiar.text: And the Philistines fought, and Israel was smitten, and they fled every man into his tent: and there was a very great slaughter; for there fell of Israel thirty thousand footmen.

verses.restored: Ark of God was captured, and two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

familiar.text: And the ark of God was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.

verses.restored: A man of Benjamin ran from battle line and came to Shiloh on that day, with garments torn and dust upon his head.

familiar.text: And there ran a man of Benjamin out of the army, and came to Shiloh the same day with his clothes rent, and with earth upon his head.

verses.restored: He came, and look, Eli was sitting upon seat beside road, watching, because his heart trembled for ark of God. The man came to tell in city, and all city cried out.

familiar.text: And when he came, lo, Eli sat upon a seat by the wayside watching: for his heart trembled for the ark of God. And when the man came into the city, and told it, all the city cried out.

verses.restored: Eli heard sound of outcry and said, What is sound of this tumult? The man hurried and came and told Eli.

familiar.text: And when Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, What meaneth the noise of this tumult? And the man came in hastily, and told Eli.

verses.restored: Eli was ninety-eight years old, and his eyes were fixed, and he was not able to see.

familiar.text: Now Eli was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were dim, that he could not see.

verses.restored: The man said to Eli, I am one who came from battle line, and I fled from battle line today. He said, What happened, my son?

familiar.text: And the man said unto Eli, I am he that came out of the army, and I fled to day out of the army. And he said, What is there done, my son?

verses.restored: The bearer of news answered and said, Israel fled before Philistines, and also a great striking was among people; also your two sons died, Hophni and Phinehas, and ark of God was captured.

familiar.text: And the messenger answered and said, Israel is fled before the Philistines, and there hath been also a great slaughter among the people, and thy two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and the ark of God is taken.

verses.restored: When he mentioned ark of God, Eli fell from upon seat backward beside gate. His neck broke, and he died, for the man was old and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when he made mention of the ark of God, that he fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died: for he was an old man, and heavy. And he had judged Israel forty years.

verses.restored: His daughter-in-law, wife of Phinehas, was pregnant, near to giving birth. She heard report that ark of God was captured and that her father-in-law and her husband had died. She bent down and gave birth, because her labor pains turned upon her.

familiar.text: And his daughter in law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to be delivered: and when she heard the tidings that the ark of God was taken, and that her father in law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and travailed; for her pains came upon her.

verses.restored: About time of her death, women standing over her said, Do not fear, for you have borne a son. But she did not answer and did not set her heart.

familiar.text: And about the time of her death the women that stood by her said unto her, Fear not; for thou hast born a son. But she answered not, neither did she regard it.

verses.restored: She called boy Ichabod, saying, Glory has gone into exile from Israel, because ark of God was captured and because of her father-in-law and her husband.

familiar.text: And she named the child Ichabod, saying, The glory is departed from Israel: because the ark of God was taken, and because of her father in law and her husband.

verses.restored: She said, Glory has gone into exile from Israel, for ark of God was captured.

familiar.text: And she said, The glory is departed from Israel: for the ark of God is taken.

translation_notes: The ark is treated by Israel's elders as a battlefield guarantee. Sacred objects, relics, scriptures, flags, and rituals must not be weaponized as magical authorization for war.
Both armies are human communities living under fear, command structures, and mass casualty. 'Philistine' must not become an ethnic slur, timeless enemy category, or pretext for modern hatred.
The Philistines' speech about 'Hebrews' and enslavement reflects wartime identity and fear. It does not define either people essentially.
Large casualty numbers require textual and historical audit and should be read as devastation, not victory metrics.
Hophni and Phinehas die in battle after abusing office; their deaths do not model vigilante justice or prove that every death reveals guilt.

Eli's blindness, age, weight, fall, broken neck, and death must not be mocked or treated as embodied proof of sin. The oracle critiques his leadership and benefit from exploitation, not disability or body size.
Phinehas's wife is unnamed but carries one of the chapter's central interpretations. Her traumatic labor and death must not be eclipsed by male military and priestly narratives.
The women tell her not to fear because she has borne a son. A newborn cannot cancel bereavement, trauma, or dying, and motherhood is not a woman's sole reason to live.
Ichabod is linked with exile/departure of glory. The naming does not make the child cursed or responsible for catastrophe.
The chapter reports ark capture as national-theological crisis but must not erase the many dead, bereaved, displaced, and traumatized people on both sides.
Divine presence cannot be possessed, transported as a weapon, or equated simplistically with institutional success.
safety_note: Do not weaponize sacred objects, glorify casualty numbers, dehumanize Philistines, or read battlefield loss as a measure of spiritual worth. Do not mock disability, age, fatness, traumatic labor, or death. Center Phinehas's wife's voice and the human cost on both sides. This is tragedy, not a template for religious warfare.
